candidates.label: Dedicated team priced per FTE
notes: base:SEL-003 favors this for: Dedicated ongoing team required
base:SEL-008 (Strong client flexibility preference) cautions: Dedicated FTE or high minimum commitment

tension_with_priorities.note: The client pays for capacity it does not use.

tradeoffs: The client pays for the team whether or not volume arrives; volume above what the team can deliver needs a change.
Early exit strands the provider's cost; a termination fee (CL-P14) shifts it.

candidates.label: Fixed-fee managed service
notes: base:SEL-003 favors this for: Dedicated ongoing team required

rules.message: A fixed fee has no overage or collar and no declared fixed scope; review whether demand is bounded.
fixed recurring fee with no allowance, overage, cap, collar, or capacity limit: provider volume exposure is unbounded

tension_with_priorities.note: The client pays for capacity it does not use.

tradeoffs: The client's spend is fixed; the provider absorbs any volume above expected unless the scope is bounded.
Early exit strands the provider's cost; a termination fee (CL-P14) shifts it.

candidates.label: Per-unit pricing with minimum spend commitment and annual fee cap
label_assumes: The minimum is below expected spend.
notes: base:SEL-008 favors this for: Strong client flexibility preference
requires_inputs: what the minimum owes on early exit: PRORATE, REMAINDER_DUE, or WAIVED
tradeoffs: The provider is protected below the minimum; the client pays for unused volume up to it.
The client's annual spend cannot exceed the cap; volume above it is the provider's cost.
Early exit strands the provider's cost; a termination fee (CL-P14) shifts it.

candidates.label: Volume-banded unit pricing with annual fee cap
label_assumes: Expected volume reaches the cheaper band.
requires_inputs: volume band boundary per contract year (each tier)
unit rate below the band boundary (each tier)
unit rate above the band boundary (each tier)
tradeoffs: The unit price falls as volume grows within the contract year; if volume falls, the client loses the cheaper band and the provider loses revenue.
The client's annual spend cannot exceed the cap; volume above it is the provider's cost.
Early exit strands the provider's cost; a termination fee (CL-P14) shifts it.

common_inputs: share of volume as a fraction (each tier)

definitions.early_exit: Who absorbs stranded cost if the client leaves early.
definitions.evidence: class A to D and prevalence as stored; WEAK when class C or D, UNVERIFIED, or no verified source.
definitions.mix: Who absorbs a shift toward complex work.
definitions.scenario volumes: Term totals: the profile's yearly figures times 24/12, rounded to whole units.
definitions.spend_variability: How the client's spend moves with volume: FIXED, BOUNDED, or VARIABLE.
definitions.volume_excess: Who absorbs volume above expected (PROVIDER works more for a fixed or capped fee; NONE_ADVERSE is paid per unit).
definitions.volume_shortfall: Who absorbs volume below expected (CLIENT pays for unused capacity; PROVIDER keeps its cost; SHARED up to a limit).

excluded.reason: A volume collar and a minimum commitment both protect the provider against a shortfall; keep one.
A termination fee and a prorated minimum are alternative early-exit terms.
The provider accepts at most SHARED volume risk.

next_step.note: Expand the candidates to compare (options.expand), fill their requires_inputs and common_inputs, then run compare_arrangements on the skeleton scenarios.

order_note: Candidates are grouped by who absorbs a volume shortfall, not ordered by preference.

warnings.message: Risk labels are pack assertions (D_PROPOSED). Fill a skeleton and run derive_risk_exposure to check them.
